import pandas as pd


def run(inputs: dict) -> dict:
    postings = inputs["postings"].copy()

    # Sort per cursor order: account_id, post_date, post_seq
    postings = postings.sort_values(
        by=["account_id", "post_date", "post_seq"],
        kind="mergesort"
    ).reset_index(drop=True)

    # Determine row validity per legacy TRY logic
    qty = postings["qty"]
    unit_price = postings["unit_price"]
    valid = qty.notna() & (qty > 0) & unit_price.notna() & (unit_price >= 0)
    postings["_valid"] = valid

    # Posted totals: only valid rows contribute, running total per account over valid rows only
    posted = postings[postings["_valid"]].copy()
    posted["post_value"] = posted["qty"] * posted["unit_price"]
    posted["running_total"] = posted.groupby("account_id")["post_value"].cumsum()

    posted_totals = posted[
        ["account_id", "post_seq", "post_date", "post_value", "running_total"]
    ].reset_index(drop=True)

    # Reject counts: per account, count invalid rows; include accounts with zero rejects
    reject_counts = (
        postings.groupby("account_id")["_valid"]
        .apply(lambda s: int((~s).sum()))
        .reset_index(name="reject_count")
    )
    reject_counts = reject_counts.sort_values("account_id", kind="mergesort").reset_index(drop=True)

    return {
        "posted_totals": posted_totals,
        "reject_counts": reject_counts,
    }
